Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We're excited to move forward with Redwood — the model performance looks strong and the team is aligned on product fit. Unfortunately, engineering ran into a pair of blockers during the onboarding sprint that have stalled our integration:

- SSO: our IdP metadata format requires one extra assertion field that your SAML connector doesn't currently accept.
- Webhooks: webhook payloads are truncated by our middleware; devs need a small header tweak from your side to preserve the full body for retries.

Both issues are in our backlog but will take our small engineering team ~2–3 weeks to complete (they're higher priority items elsewhere right now). That pushes our demo and evaluation timeline out past the current trial expiration.

Could Redwood approve a 30-day trial extension and an uplift of developer credits so our engineers can finish the end-to-end tests without being blocked on usage limits? Specifically, would you consider: 30 extra days and 15,000 free tokens for the pilot workspace?

We'd like to avoid rescheduling the executive demo — that would be awkward for our stakeholders. If you need technical specifics I can share snippets and logs (tom.ruiz@brightlayer.com is our engineering lead and can supply payload samples).

Appreciate any help here.

Best,

Hi all — dug into the samples Sarah sent. TL;DR: two separate fixes but both have short workarounds.

SSO (SAML assertion field)
- Cause: BrightLayer's IdP is sending an optional "authnContextClassRef" element nested in a custom namespace; our current SAML parser ignores unknown nested elements but in this case a downstream assert-check rejects the response.
- Workaround: we can relax the post-parsing check to tolerate the extra element for BrightLayer's tenant by adding a tenant-specific compatibility flag; that change is small (single-file change) and can be deployed to a staging slot in ~3 business days.

Webhooks: payload truncation
- Cause: BrightLayer's middleware strips Content-Length and rewrites bodies on retry; Redwood's webhook validation rejects blank body payloads.
- Workaround: if BrightLayer's middleware can forward the X-Original-Content-Length header with the retry, our webhook handler will accept the request and process the full payload. No code change required on our side.

Risk/ETA
- If BrightLayer can add X-Original-Content-Length this afternoon, we can unblock webhooks immediately.
- The tenant-compatibility flag for SSO requires a small code change + QA and is estimated 3 business days to staging, 5 business days to production (including regression testing).

Attachments: sso-debug.log (snippet), webhook-sample-payload.json (example payload)

Recommendation: approve a 30-day extension to cover the SSO rollout window and grant a 12k credits uplift so the BrightLayer engineers can complete E2E tests while we ship the SSO fix. The 12k figure is based on expected token consumption over the next 3 weeks for E2E smoke tests.

I can pair with Tom if you want a quick screen share to walk through steps tonight.

—Dev
